svg.text: Skills with the Claude API — running your custom Skills programmatically
Essence: The same Skill format runs on every Claude surface, but the Claude API does not set up the
runtime for you. You must add two things yourself — the code execution tool (a sandbox container) and the Files API.
🧩 Where Skills work across the Claude ecosystem
A Skill is a folder of instructions that Claude reads on demand. The skill files never change between
environments — but how each environment gives Claude a computer to run them does change.
Claude.ai / Desktop give Claude a container automatically. Claude Code / Agent SDK use your local files.
Only the Claude API has neither — so you provide the runtime by hand. That is what we do below.
⚠ Not shared: Skills you create in Claude.ai or Claude Desktop are not visible to the Claude API or
Claude Code. Each surface manages its own skills, so for the API we upload the skill folders again.
⚙️ The Code Execution Tool — a sandbox for Claude
Skills integrate with the Messages API through the code execution tool. This tool gives your request a
private container where Claude can run bash / shell commands and create, view, and edit files — the
exact abilities a Skill needs. Everything runs inside a safe, isolated sandbox.
• No internet connection (API only) — cannot install new packages
• Pre-installed Python libraries come out of the box
📁 The Files API — moving files in and out
The container starts empty and has no internet, so you need a way to give it files and take results
back. The Files API uploads and downloads files, and returns a file_id you use to reference each one.
writes new files to the output dir.
Take the result back out using
Anthropic's built-in skills also live in this container — ready-made helpers for pptx, pdf, xlsx, and docx.
Requirement: to use any Skill with the API you must also turn on the code execution tool.
🧪 Demo Part 1 — the Practice Question Generator skill
Goal: from a LaTeX lecture-notes file, have the skill write practice questions as a Markdown file.
Three request steps: upload the skill, upload the input file, then send the message.
# 1) Upload the skill folder — you get back a skill_id
# 2) Upload the input file — you get back a file object with an id
# 3) Send the message — skills go in "container", tools enable code execution
# three beta headers are always needed together: skills · code-execution · files-api
What Claude did in the container — progressive disclosure
Progressive disclosure means Claude reads SKILL.md first, and only opens extra files (like the template)
when the task actually needs them. This keeps the context small. Finally you download the file by its id.
Demo Part 2 — combine a custom skill with a built-in one
Now analyze a retail sales CSV with a custom time-series skill, then write the results as a Word document
using Anthropic's built-in docx skill. You can list several skills in one container.
# mix a custom skill (by id) with a built-in Anthropic skill (by name)
# same three beta headers as before: skills · code-execution · files-api
• Examined the first 20 lines of the CSV
• Ran the skill's diagnostics + visualize scripts
• Built the .docx with the built-in skill
• Copied it out → downloaded by file_id
Deleting a skill — versions first, then the skill
# a skill can have many versions — delete each version, then the skill itself
• Always send the three beta headers together — skills, code-execution, files-api — or the request fails.
• The skill folder is uploaded once and reused by skill_id; pick a version or use "latest".
• Remember there is no internet in the API container — depend only on pre-installed libraries.
• The skill files are identical to Claude.ai; only the wiring around them (container + Files API) differs.
• Evaluate the output against what the skill promised, then edit the skill and re-upload to improve it.
• Skills are managed through the /v1/skills endpoint (client.beta.skills), which handles upload,
versioning, listing, and deletion of custom skills — separate from the built-in Anthropic skills.
• The code execution tool is still the required runtime for Skills; each request provisions a fresh container.
• Built-in skills for pptx, pdf, xlsx, and docx ship ready to use — no upload needed, just name them.
🔑 Key insight: A Skill is just instructions — it does nothing without a computer to run on. Claude.ai hands
Claude that computer for free; on the API you build it from the code execution tool plus the Files API.
